summary.intent: Execute all 8 plans in phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) using wave-based parallel execution, then run the full ship-phase loop (verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E → CodeRabbit → PR).
summary.outcome: All 8 plans executed across 4 waves with gates passing; a ship-blocking SDK E2E regression from plan 60-05 was caught and fixed; 7 additional security hardening fixes from CodeRabbit triage were applied; 27/27 threats verified closed in SECURITY.md; the phase is ready to ship pending the one parens-subject commit reword, push, and PR open.

repo: Ed25519 IPNS records do NOT embed the public key in the record protobuf bytes — it lives in the IPNS name (k51…). The old `withCachedPublicKey` enrich in ipns.service.ts supplied pubKey from the DB's `publicKey` column; 60-05 removed it on the false assumption it was embedded, breaking every strict publish→resolve round-trip.

The SDK E2E test harness (test-harness.ts) generates accounts with `email = ...-${Date.now()}@example.com`, making each run use unique IPNS names — stale-DB collisions are impossible, so an E2E failure is always a real round-trip regression, not a dirty-state artifact.

API unit tests mocked `parseIpnsRecord` to include `pubKey`, masking the real Ed25519 behavior where the function returns no pubKey. That blind spot let 60-05's regression pass 172 jest tests and only surface in the SDK E2E gate.
lint-staged only handles .ts/.json/.md files — .rs files are never auto-formatted on commit, so Rust edits land in the committed hand-written style regardless of workspace rustfmt settings.

`cargo fmt --check` across the workspace reports drift caused by a local rustfmt version mismatch (not real drift introduced by edits). Running blanket `cargo fmt` would spuriously reformat files the phase never touched; don't do it.

The GSD commit helper regularly reports `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands (lint-staged exit noise). Always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying — blind retry creates duplicate commits.

1Password SSH signer (`op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`) wedges after a rapid burst of signed commits. Recovery: quit and reopen the 1Password desktop app (or toggle Settings → Developer → SSH agent off/on). Staged changes survive — only the signer is stuck, not the working tree.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL restriction). PR body patches must go through `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.

decode_ipns_cbor_validity in crates/core used first-wins behavior for duplicate 'Validity' CBOR keys, while its sibling decode_ipns_cbor_data explicitly rejected duplicates with a parser-differential attack guard. The inconsistency was a real security gap (D-07 fail-closed scope).

registry.rs register_device swallowed ALL fetch errors (including VerifyError::Invalid for tampered records) and treated them as the 'first device' bootstrap path, auto-authorizing the device. Only HTTP 404 (ApiError::IpnsNotFound) is a legitimate bootstrap signal.

code.finding: resolveRecord returns the bare network result (from parseIpnsRecordBytes) on equal-sequence — loses sig fields for Ed25519 records where pubKey isn't in the record bytes. Fix: serve the authoritative DB cachedResult on equal-or-higher sequence so the strict client always receives a verifiable record.

Strict resolve requires pubKey in the response and verifies deriveIpnsName(pubKey) === ipnsName; throws 'fail closed' when all three sig fields are absent. This is the layer that surfaced the 60-05 regression.

TS resolve path skipped EOL enforcement when Validity was not a Uint8Array (absent field silently accepted). Rust ipns.rs:114-117 fail-closes on absent Validity via .ok_or_else(). Fixed to mirror Rust: absent Validity now throws fail-closed (D-07 cross-layer parity).

decode_ipns_cbor_validity used early-return first-wins for duplicate 'Validity' keys; sibling decode_ipns_cbor_data rejects duplicates. A crafted record with two Validity entries decoded ambiguously across parsers, undermining fail-closed EOL enforcement. Fixed to accumulate + reject on second occurrence.

Broad `Err(_) => None` swallowed VerifyError::Invalid (tampered/expired registry), triggering first-device bootstrap with auto-authorization. Fixed to only bootstrap on `SdkError::Api(ApiError::IpnsNotFound)`; all other errors propagate (D-08 fail-closed).

parse_rfc3339_to_unix_secs had three leniencies: trailing components accepted silently, impossible dates (2026-02-31) passed day validation and rolled forward via Hinnant civil_from_days, extending record validity. Fixed with strict component count checks and leap-aware day-of-month validation.
Verify cache was unbounded (no max size), risking memory exhaustion under load. Fixed with LRU eviction bounded to MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES.

Vault-settings sequence fallback swallowed all resolveIpnsRecord errors (including strict verification throws) and treated them as 'no existing record'. Fixed to only bootstrap on null return (true not-found); all thrown errors propagate.
Accounts are uniquely keyed per run via Date.now() in the email, so SDK E2E failures always represent real round-trip regressions — stale-data collision is structurally impossible.

workflow: The SDK E2E gate is the only suite that exercises the real client→API IPNS publish/resolve round-trip. All 343 unit/integration tests (Rust + jest + sdk-core vitest) mock the boundary and would have shipped a broken strict-verify regression. The gate caught 28/89 failures that no other suite detected.

Sequential gsd-executor subagents on the main working tree (vs worktree isolation with merge) is the safer mode for a security-critical phase with strict cross-plan dependencies — each executor commits and verifies in order, preventing merge conflicts on shared interfaces.

Running an adversarial triage workflow against CodeRabbit findings (15 findings → 7 fix-now, 4 defer-todo, 4 false-positive) efficiently prevented both over-fixing (the pre-increment-sequence false positives) and under-fixing (the 7 real security gaps).
When a GSD executor's SUMMARY update is committed but its ROADMAP checkbox isn't ticked, reconcile manually with a targeted commit rather than re-running the executor.
Running `cargo test --workspace` from the orchestrator (not a subagent) before a non-autonomous operational cutover provides authoritative, unambiguous gate evidence for the cutover-readiness record.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged mid-session (`op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`) after a rapid burst of 28 phase commits, blocking all subsequent commits until the desktop app was restarted.

GSD commit helper false-negatives (reports `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands) required `git log` verification after every commit to avoid duplicate retries — happened 4+ times across the session.
`cargo fmt --check` reported workspace-wide drift caused by a local rustfmt version mismatch, creating noise and requiring investigation to confirm the drift was pre-existing and safe to ignore.
TS commits backgrounded by the orchestrator were silently dropped mid-sequence when the background process was cut off, requiring detection via `git log` and manual re-issue of the remaining commits.

60-05's unit test explicitly codified the buggy behavior (asserting signatureV2/data are undefined on equal-seq), meaning the test suite not only missed the regression but actively locked it in — required updating the test to assert correct behavior.
The stale mid-edit compile diagnostic (`VerifyError::Legacy not found`) at the end of 60-01 caused a false alarm that required an explicit `cargo check` run to disprove.
CodeRabbit CLI review output was truncated in the task result (27,331 chars cut), requiring a secondary full-file read to get all patch instructions.
